GmailDraft.description: Gmail REST draft resource (an id plus its draft message).

GmailMessage.description:
A Gmail message resource.

Populated fields depend on the requested [`GmailMessageFormat`]:
`payload` comes with the full format, `raw` with the raw format.

historyId.description: The id of the last history record that modified the message.

id.description: The immutable id of the message.

internalDate.description:
The internal message creation timestamp (epoch milliseconds),
which determines ordering in the inbox.

labelIds.description: The ids of the labels applied to the message.

payload.description: The parsed email structure in the message parts.

raw.description: The entire message as a base64url-encoded RFC 5322 string.

sizeEstimate.description: The estimated size of the message in bytes.

snippet.description: A short part of the message text.

threadId.description: The id of the thread the message belongs to.

GmailMessageHeader.description: A single header of a Gmail message part.

GmailMessagePartBody.description: The body of a single MIME part of a Gmail message.

attachmentId.description:
The id of an external attachment, retrievable via a separate
`users.messages.attachments.get` request.

data.description:
The body data as a base64url-encoded string; absent when the
data lives in an external attachment.

size.description: The number of bytes of the message part data.

body.description:
The body of the part, which may be empty for container MIME
parts.

filename.description:
The filename of the attachment; empty when the part is not an
attachment.

headers.description: The headers of the part, such as To, From or Subject.

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the part.

partId.description: The immutable id of the message part.

parts.description: The child parts of a container MIME part.

description:
Wraps a renderable listing with an optional pagination cursor so the
"next page" hint is part of the command output: a trailing footer
line in text mode, an extra `next_page` field in JSON. This keeps
the cursor visible to scripts, unlike logging it to stderr.
title: Paginated
